Research notes, Incomar.

Created because the-interface.md names it as one of five console makers Hy-Tek's Meet
Manager could talk to in 1988. It is the thinnest of the five by a wide margin and the page
says so.

Everything found, and it is not much:
  - sources/periodicals/swimming-technique/198011.txt:2796 and 198102.txt:2640 list
    "Incomar - Pacing System" in a supplier directory of the kind that gives a company and a
    product category and nothing else. The 198102 line is a run-together list of about
    twenty suppliers, so the pairing of Incomar with pacing system is the only content.
  - sources/periodicals/swimming-world/198104.txt:34642 is an advertiser index entry, just
    the name.
  - sources/periodicals/swimming-world/198808.txt:1032 is the one that matters: Hy-Tek's
    announcement that Meet Manager would interface with consoles from Omega, Daktronics,
    Kyrotech, Incomar and Colorado.

That is the whole trail in the periodicals. No address, no contact, no product name beyond
"pacing system", no advertisement copy, and nothing in the held vendor collection.

But the product name survives elsewhere, and this is the find. Hy-Tek's current Meet
Manager 8 user guide lists "Incomar Splash 1" among the timing consoles it interfaces with,
in the group that cannot take an event download, and gives it a topic page of its own at
incomar.htm (hytek.active.com/user_guides_html/swmm8/timingconsoleinterface.htm, checked
September 2026). Read that topic page before building this out; it is the fullest
description of the product in reach.

The gap is closed, and the answer was in the corpus all along. A display advertisement runs
in at least five issues between 1980 and 1981 (swimming-technique/198005.txt:1998-2002 and
198008.txt:3654 and 198011.txt:4167 and 198102.txt:3326; swimming-world/198104.txt:28200)
and it names the product: INCOMAR'S New SPLASH I SMARTY Pacing System, from INCOMAR, 4996
Southview, Utica, Michigan 48087, telephone (313) 731-0177. So the pacing system of 1980
and the console Hy-Tek listed in 1988 carry the same name, and an earlier draft of this
page was wrong twice over: it said the corpus gave no address, no telephone and no product
name beyond "pacing system", and it said the Splash 1 was a name no magazine here records.
All three are in the advertisement.

What is still open is narrower than it was. A pacing system and a timing console are
different kinds of product, and nothing held explains how one became the other, or whether
Hy-Tek's "console" is loose usage. The shared name is now evidence for continuity rather
than a coincidence, but it is not proof of it.

Spelling was checked. The earlier sweep for Incomar missed the display advertisement above,
which is a caution about declaring a corpus search exhausted: the hits it did find were all
index and directory lines, and the advertisement sits in a page of display copy that a
narrower grep passed over.

Still to research: what the company was called in full and where it was; what the Meet

This article is a stub. Incomar, of Utica, Michigan, advertised the Splash I "Smarty"
pacing system in the American swimming press in 1980 and 1981, and in 1988 Hy-Tek listed
the company among the five console makers its Meet Manager software would connect to.

The magazines carry nothing at all after 1988, but the product outlived the coverage:
Hy-Tek's current documentation still lists the Splash 1 among the timers
[Meet Manager](../software/hy-tek-meet-manager.md) will talk to. See
[The Interface](../software/the-interface.md) for the 1988 announcement and the
[vendors](index.md) register for the companies this wiki covers.
